How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough but the process of getting housing was not impressive. The organisation of student housing only answered on whether you got housing through the host institution a week or two before arrival - if you were lucky enough to get housing. This was also the experience of many other exchange students i met.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Student housing helps you get started socially but also takes some patience in terms of difference in living standards.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A little confusing and I didn't get all the courses I wanted, but in the end I was happy about the courses I got.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to choose what courses you wanted but still had to be ready at a specific date to actually register for these courses and the best courses were quickly taken.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Pretty much zero although you could email some from the host institution if you had questions about the courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Didn't get all I wanted but I was happy with the ones I got

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do some research before you have to register and have a plan b and c.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Really not impressive. The academic level was quite low and so was the expectations of the students. Small level of engagement from fellow students as well.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had Plan, kultur og næring where the general expectation of the students was very low because it was a 1. semester course. My other courses (Artic Norway - Aspects of Culture and Arctic Norway - Aspects of Politics) simply didn't seem to care much about student engagement.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's hard to compare because most of my time at KU has been with online teaching because of corona but in general the level of teaching was much higher. The style at KU also gives the students better chances at engaging in discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Plan kulture og næring | Arctic Norway - Aspects of Culture | Arctic Norway - Aspects of Politics, international relations and governments

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed learning about the area where I was on exchange (the two about arctic norway) also having a course that was more of a local course (PLN) helped me meet more norwegian students which gave a great experience socially but mostly for non-academic reasons

questions.answer: Way too much to mention here. Go to TSI's webside.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Everything that gives you a chance at exploring the outdoors around Tromsø.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Lyngen, Sommerøy, Senja and if you have a chance (and the money) go to Svalbard. Explore the mountains. There are cabins in the area that you can reserve. It's a great way to go for a weekend-long hike or skiing trip. But when it's not too cold yet I would recommend going camping. Turbo is a little shop in the city center where you can rent everything for free for camping, skiing and even bikes. Nabobil is an app where you can rent private cars for cheap money which makes it easier to go on weekend trips away from Tromsø.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join sport teams and other communities for recreational activities

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Norwegians can be very reserved but are usually very nice, polite and helpfull if you are too

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Same as mentioned above.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go exploring, be social early and get a membership at pust (sauna)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: D vitamins are good when it starts to get a bit too dark

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the things a experienced. Mostly through outdoor activities and the people a got to know

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To save up for a trip to Svalbard. I did not succeed.

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
